predecessors.name: Syrian Arab Republic under the Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party
predecessors.text: Syria as drawn by Cliopatria's 'Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party' row (1967-1972), the same cells as this row's 1973 shape

ledger.x: 1973: Cliopatria's 'Syria' row begins over the cells of its Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party row; the Syrian Arab Republic has stood since the end of the French mandate and this is a row boundary, not a founding.
ledger.cpn: Syrian Arab Republic under the Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party

ledger.x: Carried over from the predecessor dossier: Israel has held the Golan Heights since June 1967 ('the Israel Defense Forces captured the Golan Heights on [9-10 June]'; 1,070 km2 of the Heights proper and 100 km2 of the Hermon slopes).
6 October 1973: Syria and Egypt attack Israel and the Golan front opens.
25 October 1973: the fighting ends.
1974: Quneitra returns to Syria.
31 May 1976: the Syrian army enters Lebanon.
October 1976: Syria takes central Lebanon.
14 December 1981: Israel passes the Golan Heights Law, ending the military occupation of the Golan in favour of annexation.
14 December 1981: Israel annexes the Golan.
30 April 2005: Syria completes its withdrawal from Lebanon.
30 April 2005: Syria leaves central Lebanon as well (same sentence).
2012: the Kurdish-led autonomous region takes shape in the north-east.
ledger.cpn: Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria

ledger.x: 2013: rebels take Raqqa.
2014: the Islamic State takes eastern Syria.

2015: rebels take Idlib, the second provincial capital they win ('capturing the regional capitals of Raqqa in 2013 and Idlib in 2015'); the Syria page adds that Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham later consolidated the rebel groups in 'its stronghold in northwestern Syria'.
May 2015: the Islamic State at its greatest extent.
2016: the government retakes Aleppo.
August 2016: Turkey invades northern Syria.
17 October 2017: the Kurdish-led SDF capture Raqqa from the Islamic State.
ledger.cpn: Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria

ledger.x: January-March 2018: government forces advance in Ghouta.
January-March 2018: Turkey takes Afrin.
23 March 2019: the Islamic State loses its last land in Syria.
ledger.cpn: Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria

ledger.x: September-December 2019: Turkey enters north-eastern Syria.
29 November 2024: the opposition offensive begins.
8 December 2024: the Assad government falls.
8 December 2024: Assad's government is replaced.
December 2024: Israel enters the Golan buffer zone.

wars.name: Yom Kippur War
wars.outcome: Syria gained ground in the southern Golan, was pushed back to the Purple Line and then lost 500 km2 of the Bashan region to an Israeli counteroffensive; the ceasefire of 25 October 1973 was followed by the 1974 disengagement agreement that restored Quneitra…

wars.name: Syrian occupation of Lebanon
wars.outcome: Syria entered Lebanon on 31 May 1976 under the cover of the Arab Deterrent Force, took central Lebanon in October 1976, occupied the presidential palace at Baabda on 13 October 1990 and withdrew completely on 30 April 2005.

wars.name: Syrian civil war
wars.outcome: Demonstrations began on 26 January 2011; rebels, the Islamic State (to 23 March 2019), the Kurdish-led administration and Turkey each took land; by 2021 the government held about two-thirds of the country; after the March 2020 ceasefire the front froze until…

certainty.note: Judgment, not read from a page: Syria's international frontiers are treaty or armistice lines.

From the civil war the control lines between the government, the opposition, the Islamic State, the Kurdish-led administration and Turkey are fronts, not borders; the external frontier stays as in 2010.
